references.label: Reconfigurable Photonic Braids
references.title: Give an algebraic operation a traversable physical route.
references.paper: Reconfigurable non-Abelian integrated photonics
references.mechanism: A tunable photonic building block implements mode transformations through ordered couplings; connected blocks realize reconfigurable braiding operations.
trace: Trace one input waveguide through the layered chip rather than beginning with the matrix notation.
Zoom into b: follow steps I, II and III through the coupling regions and the auxiliary path.
Map that repeated physical block to the compact operation sequence in c.
references.lesson: Gray waveguides establish the substrate, blue/red distinguish layers and couplings, and gold control traces connect visible electrodes to precise regions. A close-up resolves the local operation before a compact algebraic summary.
references.borrow: Place the operator on the substrate that carries it; use an enlarged local view to make the global algebra physically traceable.
references.check: Can the reader identify which local control changes which state transformation, and trace the order of composed operations?
references.avoid: Do not interpret a drawn crossing as literal mode exchange without the coupling model; a braid-like shape alone is not evidence of non-Abelian behavior.
references.limit: This is a device/operation schematic. The non-Abelian claim and reconfiguration performance rely on the paper’s model and measurements, not the appearance of crossed lines.
references.approval: curator selection of 2026-10-08

references.label: Plenoxels
references.title: A ray crosses a voxel grid, and each sample blends the eight corners of its voxel.
references.paper: Plenoxels: Radiance Fields without Neural Networks
references.mechanism: A scene is a sparse grid of voxels. Each grid corner stores a density and spherical-harmonic coefficients. A sample on a camera ray reads a trilinear blend of the eight corners round it, and the samples on the ray integrate to one pixel colour.
trace: Panel a: follow the ray from the camera through the training image into the sparse grid. One voxel is solid blue.
Panel b: that voxel, enlarged. The orange arrows bring the values of the eight corners to the sample on the ray.
Panel c: the samples on the ray become a density curve and one predicted colour.
references.lesson: One ray is the persistent object. It keeps its direction and its style from the scene, to the enlarged voxel, to the plot. The zoom is a blue cone that starts at the marked voxel. The grid is dots and dashes, so it gives structure and no clutter.
references.borrow: Carry one sample through the full method. Keep its line in the same direction in each panel. Enlarge the one cell where the operation occurs, and join the two views with a cone.
references.check: Can the reader follow one line from the input to the output with no break?
references.limit: The right third is flat and holds a formula. The figure shows one ray. The optimisation over all rays is one line of text.
references.approval: curator selection of 2026-11-13, not yet reviewed by the user

references.label: Flagellar motor stator
references.title: With the stator in place, protons flow and the stator grips the rotor ring.
references.paper: Structural insights into flagellar stator–rotor interactions
references.mechanism: Sixteen stator units insert between the collar and the C-ring of the motor. Protons go through each stator, and the stator touches the FliG ring of the rotor, where the torque is made.
trace: Compare the top row (no stator, ΔmotB) with the bottom row (wild type). The yellow stator units appear in the bottom row only.
Columns C and G: a cut through the motor. In G, follow the arrow of H+ through the stator.
Columns D and H: the C-ring from the side. In H, the stator touches the green ring.
references.lesson: Two rows and four cameras that are the same in each row. The intervention has one colour, yellow, and it is absent in the top row. A background tint names the condition of each row. The zoom goes from the whole, to the cut, to the contact.
references.borrow: Put a mutant or an ablation in the top row and the full system in the bottom row. Keep the cameras the same. Give the added part one colour.
references.check: Is the added part the only difference between the rows?
references.limit: The maps are densities from electron tomography of cells. The proton path is an interpretation.
references.approval: curator selection of 2026-11-13, not yet reviewed by the user

references.label: São Jorge dike intrusion
references.title: Magma rises from the mantle along an old fault and stalls below the island.
references.paper: Fault-mediated magma propagation and triggered seismicity revealed by the 2022 São Jorge Azores unrest
references.mechanism: Melt collects in the mantle. A dike opens and rises fast through a fault zone that was there before. It stalls at the base of the island, and fluids that escape from it cause earthquakes along the fault.
trace: Read the block: the island surface is on top, and the depth scale is on the right edge.
Follow the green numbers 1 to 7 from the bottom to the top. The dashed arrows show the rise of the dike.
The question marks show what the data does not fix.
references.lesson: One block joins the map view and the section. Numbers give the sequence of events inside the space. The orange body is the one saturated shape. Question marks keep the uncertain parts honest.
references.borrow: Cut a block. Put the process on its faces. Number the events in time sequence. Mark what is not certain.
references.check: Can the reader tell the sequence with no caption, and tell the certain from the uncertain?
references.limit: An interpretation. The depth axis is not linear. The labels are many and long.
references.approval: curator selection of 2026-11-13, not yet reviewed by the user

references.label: Tomographic volumetric printing
references.title: Light patterns from many angles add up to a solid part inside a rotating vial.
references.paper: High-resolution tomographic volumetric additive manufacturing
references.mechanism: A modulator sends a different light pattern into a rotating vial of resin for each angle. The dose adds up in the volume and the part becomes solid. A second beam at 90 degrees observes the part.
trace: Start at the DLP modulator at the left. Follow the blue beam through the two lenses to the vial.
Look at the strip of projections below the modulator: one pattern for each angle of the vial.
Find the part inside the yellow resin. Then follow the red beam to the camera, which observes the part from the side.
references.lesson: One optical axis runs across the page, and each element sits on it in its real sequence. The beams are translucent volumes, so the eye sees where the light is. Two colours separate two jobs: blue writes and red observes. The container is a ghost, so the part inside it stays visible.
references.borrow: Put the full apparatus on one axis in one camera. Draw the thing that travels (light, fluid, signal) as a translucent volume with its own colour. Use a second colour for a second path that has a different job.
references.check: Can a reader point to where the energy enters, where it acts and where it is measured?
references.limit: The figure shows the apparatus. The accumulation of dose, which is the core of the method, is implied by the projection strip and is not drawn.
references.approval: curator selection of 2026-11-13, not yet reviewed by the user

references.label: Coordinate-independent convolution
references.title: Move a kernel along two paths: on a plane it agrees, on a sphere it rotates, on a Möbius strip it flips.
references.paper: Coordinate Independent Convolutional Networks: Isometry and Gauge Equivariant Convolutions on Riemannian Manifolds
references.mechanism: On a curved or non-orientable surface, the alignment of a convolution kernel depends on the path along which it moves. Thus the network must give the same result for each choice of local frame.
trace: Figure 3: on each surface, follow the red path and the green path from the same start kernel to the same end point.
Compare the two kernels that arrive, in the row at the bottom: identity, rotation, flip.
Figure 27: the Möbius strip is cut into two charts and unrolled. Find where the charts agree (id) and where they differ (flip).
references.lesson: A matched counterfactual on three surfaces: only the surface changes. The kernel is a small image with a frame, so its orientation is readable at once. Soft grey surfaces with contact shadows keep all attention on the coloured paths. The lizard and the butterfly in figures 23 and 27 are asymmetric motifs, so a flip or a rotation is obvious.
references.borrow: To show that a space changes an operation, do the same operation on three spaces with the same camera. Use an asymmetric motif when orientation matters. Unroll the surface when the reader must see its charts.
references.check: Would the reader see the difference if the motif were symmetric? If not, change the motif.
references.limit: The notation in figures 23 and 27 is dense for a reader outside the field. The figures are formal illustrations and are not data.
references.approval: curator selection of 2026-11-13, not yet reviewed by the user

references.label: Scutoids in Curved Tissue
references.title: Let a change of neighbors become a three-dimensional shape.
references.paper: Scutoids are a geometrical solution to three-dimensional packing of epithelia
references.mechanism: Packing between differently curved apical and basal surfaces can involve neighbor exchanges along cell depth; a scutoid has a vertex arrangement that permits such a transition.
trace: Compare the prism and frustum assumptions in a–b with the nested apical/basal surfaces in c.
Follow the same colored cells between the two surfaces; identify which neighboring relationships change.
Inspect d and g: the extra vertex and triangular face give that neighbor transition a physical geometry.
references.lesson: Persistent cell colors connect the inner/outer tilings to isolated three-dimensional pieces; translucent surfaces reveal depth without hiding the interface that changes.
references.borrow: Show adjacency-changing structure through linked sections and one extracted local interface, not only a flattened graph.
references.check: Can the reader point to the vertex/face where a neighboring relationship changes through depth?
references.avoid: Do not import a scutoid shape into an unrelated graph merely because topology is involved; the geometric packing relation must be real.
references.limit: This figure develops a geometric model and examples of packing; it does not imply every curved epithelium has one universal cell geometry. The beetle panel is a naming analogy, not mechanistic evidence.
references.approval: curator selection of 2026-10-08

references.label: GraphCast
references.title: The world stays visible while the representation changes.
references.paper: Learning skillful medium-range global weather forecasting
references.mechanism: A graph network maps weather fields onto a spherical multimesh, exchanges information, and decodes the next weather state.
trace: Find the same globe at input and forecast output.
In d and f, trace grid points into mesh nodes and back again.
In g, compare short and long mesh edges: different spatial reaches belong to one processor.
references.lesson: Earth remains visible through grid, mesh and output. Enlargements expose the transfers; the lower mesh row makes scale differences directly comparable.
references.borrow: Keep the physical substrate visible when it explains the graph and its interactions.
references.check: Can the reader locate where information enters, travels and returns? Verify the actual graph adjacency and coordinate transforms.
references.avoid: Do not replace an arbitrary latent graph with a globe unless its geometry is genuinely spatial.
references.limit: The graph depicts learned communication, not literal atmospheric transport. Forecast validity requires separate evaluation.

references.label: Hopfion in a multilayer
references.title: A quarter cut shows how the spins turn inside two magnetic textures.
references.paper: Creation and observation of Hopfions in magnetic multilayer systems
references.mechanism: A target skyrmion has the same spin pattern at each height. A hopfion has a ring of twisted spins in the middle layers only. A surface-sensitive X-ray method and a bulk method thus give different images for the hopfion.
trace: Top cylinder, target skyrmion: on the two cut faces, the arrow pattern is the same at each height.
Bottom cylinder, hopfion: on the cut faces, the arrows turn round a ring in the middle and stay vertical at the top and the bottom.
At the right, compare the two predicted X-ray images for each texture. The two methods differ for the hopfion only.
references.lesson: The same quarter cut and the same camera for the two states make the texture the only thing that changes. The cut faces carry the field, so the inside becomes readable. The layer stack at the left ties each texture to the structure that hosts it.
references.borrow: To compare two internal states, cut the two bodies with the same planes and view them with the same camera. Put the field on the cut faces.
references.check: Does the difference between the states show on the cut faces with no caption?
references.limit: The typography and the panel letters are rough. The arrow colours have no legend. The textures come from a model.
references.approval: curator selection of 2026-11-13, not yet reviewed by the user

references.label: Type III secretion needle
references.title: Cut the needle complex in half to see the substrate in the channel.
references.paper: Substrate-engaged type III secretion system structures reveal gating mechanism for unfolded protein translocation
references.mechanism: The injectisome moves an unfolded protein from the base, through the export apparatus and up the channel of the needle, into the host cell.

references.label: Vector-field electron tomography
references.title: Two tilt series and one constraint give the full 3D magnetic field.
references.paper: Unveiling the three-dimensional magnetic texture of skyrmion tubes
references.mechanism: The sample tilts about two axes. Each tilt series gives phase images, and each set of images gives one component of the magnetic induction as a volume. The condition of zero divergence gives the third component.
trace: In the centre, find the needle sample in the hole of the holder, and the phase image that it projects below.
At the left and the right, the holder tilts about x and about y. Each series gives one component, Bx or By, as a volume.
Follow the grey triangles to the equation. Zero divergence gives Bz, and panel b shows the full field.
references.lesson: The geometry of the measurement is the figure. Each data product sits below the physical setup that makes it, thus the layout is the pipeline. Colour identity holds: red is the x series and blue is the y series, in the axes, the labels and the equation.
references.borrow: When a result comes from several measurements, draw each measurement as a physical scene and put its data directly below it. Join the data products at the equation that combines them.
references.check: Can the reader say which measurement gives which component of the result?
references.limit: The small arrows in the central disc are dense. The steps between a phase image and a volume are not shown.
references.approval: curator selection of 2026-11-13, not yet reviewed by the user

references.label: Biomimetic 4D Printing
references.title: Translate a target shape into the local directions that create it.
references.paper: Biomimetic 4D printing
references.mechanism: A spatially programmed print path controls anisotropic swelling; local orientation patterns are chosen so hydration bends a flat printed structure toward a desired shape.
trace: Move from the natural form in a to its mathematical surface and extracted curvatures in b–c.
Compare the two print-path directions in d with the predicted structure in e.
Read the fabricated before/after states in f as the consequence of that local programming.
references.lesson: A consistent silhouette connects nature, mathematical geometry, directional paths and a glowing physical lattice; shared contours do more work than generic arrows or prose.
references.borrow: Let one recognizable global form pass through its geometric decomposition, local program and actual physical response.
references.check: Can the reader connect a local direction in the program to a region of the final curvature?
references.avoid: Do not use a flower as a general symbol for growth; retain it only when its geometry is the design input.
references.limit: The illustrated specimen and model demonstrate the stated material/printing system, not universal shape programmability for any material or arbitrary loading condition.
references.approval: curator selection of 2026-10-08

references.label: Cascading lake drainage
references.title: A lake that drains opens crevasses and speeds up the ice in a chain.
references.paper: Cascading lake drainage on the Greenland Ice Sheet triggered by tensile shock and fracture
references.mechanism: Water from the surface reaches the bed and the ice above speeds up. The stress at a lake changes from compression to tension. A crevasse opens, the lake drains, and the new water at the bed starts the same process at the next lake.
trace: Panel a: a block of the ice sheet with a lake, a moulin and water at the bed. Red shows acceleration.
Panels b to d: the same block at later times. Follow the blue water as it reaches the bed at new places.
The small box below each block gives the sign of the stress at the lake.
references.lesson: The same block in four states with one camera. Two colours with fixed meanings: blue is water and red is faster flow. A small stress glyph below each state gives the cause, in the same position each time.
references.borrow: Repeat one block for each stage. Keep two colours for two quantities. Put a small glyph for the cause in the same place in each stage.
references.check: Does each stage differ from the stage before it by one event?
references.limit: Schematic with vertical exaggeration. The labels are dense in panel d.

references.label: Tokamak control
references.title: Cut the vessel open: coils outside, plasma inside, and the section that the controller shapes.
references.paper: Magnetic control of tokamak plasmas through deep reinforcement learning
references.mechanism: Rings of coils surround a vacuum vessel. Their currents shape the plasma in the vessel. The controller sets the coil voltages to hold the plasma boundary, the X-point and the legs at their targets.
trace: Panel g: the nested rings are the coils. A wedge is cut away, and the plasma shows in the two cut faces.
Follow the dashed lines from the right cut face to panel h.
Panel h: the flat cross-section with the plasma boundary, the X-point and the legs. These are the control targets.
references.lesson: The cutaway shows where things are. The flat section shows what to measure. Dashed lines join one cut face to the flat panel, so the reader knows that the two are the same plane.
references.borrow: Cut the body to show the inside. Then draw one cut face flat and large, and put the exact labels there. Join the two views with lines.
references.check: Does the flat panel match a cut face that the reader can find in the 3D view?
references.limit: The first image is a crop. In the full figure, the control loops are boxes and arrows.

references.label: Computational Caustics
references.title: Make the desired image become a physical ray map.
references.paper: High-contrast Computational Caustic Design
references.mechanism: A transport map from source to target irradiance specifies surface normals; surface optimization produces a refractor whose light distribution approximates the target.
trace: Locate the light source, transparent surface and receiving screen; keep their roles distinct.
Follow the target irradiance backwards into the transport assignment and the corresponding surface-normal field.
Use related Figure 1 to connect the optimized physical acrylic surface with the projected caustic as it rotates.
references.lesson: The same receiver plane makes source and target distributions comparable; ray direction, normal direction and physical surface remain attached, not split into abstract module names.
references.borrow: Expose the inverse map from a desired field to local controls, then return to a measured physical consequence.
references.check: Can the reader explain how changing one local surface region changes a particular part of the received pattern?
references.avoid: Do not borrow ray geometry for a process with no defensible transport mapping, or imply exact image recovery from an illustrative example.
references.limit: The surface is an optimized approximation under an optical model. Target imagery and physical photographs have their own rights and are not new evidence for another project.
references.approval: curator selection of 2026-10-08

references.label: NeRF
references.title: Follow one ray all the way to one pixel.
references.paper: NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis
references.mechanism: A learned field supplies density and view-dependent color; volume rendering accumulates these along camera rays.

Follow its sampled locations into color and density in b, then the depth profile in c.
Find the corresponding pixel comparison in d: the chain ends in an observable residual.
references.lesson: The same rays connect a physical scene to sampled density/color, depth profiles and a pixel residual. Small labels describe the quantity at each transformation.

references.check: Can every stage's output be matched to the next stage's input? Verify the actual reduction, units and weighting.

references.label: K-Planes
references.title: A point in space and time is read from six planes.
references.paper: K-Planes: Explicit Radiance Fields in Space, Time, and Appearance
references.mechanism: A 4D field factorises into six planes: three for space and three that pair one space axis with time. A sample is projected onto each plane, read by bilinear interpolation at several scales, and the six readings are multiplied.
trace: Find the sample q on the ray from the camera.
Follow q to its projections on the three space planes xy, xz, yz and on the three space-time planes.
Panel b: on each plane, the four grid values round the projection are blended at two scales. Panel c multiplies the six results.
references.lesson: The planes stand in 3D in their real orientation, thus the factorisation is a visible fact and not only an equation. The same point q appears on each plane with the same mark.
references.borrow: When a method factorises a volume, draw the factors as planes or lines in their real orientation and project one sample onto each.
references.check: Does one sample appear on each factor with the same mark?
references.limit: The two triads of planes overlap and are dense. Read the image at full size.

references.label: RFdiffusion
references.title: Keep the constraint visible while structure emerges.
references.paper: De novo design of protein structure and function with RFdiffusion
references.mechanism: Iterative denoising constructs protein backbones; conditioning supplies symmetry, a binding target or a fixed motif that constrains what the trajectory can become.
trace: Read the noising/reverse-generative sequence in a, then identify the fixed conditioning object in each row of b.
Follow each row’s persistent motif or symmetry through the intermediate structures into the final backbone.
Compare the noisy input row with the clean-structure prediction row at matched denoising steps in c.
references.lesson: Rows are organized by a visible conditioning object; restrained, persistent colors distinguish fixed motifs from evolving structure. Matched temporal columns turn a complicated model into an inspectable transformation.
references.borrow: Use aligned state sequences in which the protected or conditioning object remains recognizable throughout the update.
references.check: Can a reader identify the unchanged constraint and distinguish the current state from its clean-state prediction?
references.avoid: Do not copy protein imagery for a non-structural problem or imply that a smooth denoising sequence alone validates a designed function.
references.limit: The figure describes model construction and examples. Structural plausibility and predicted designability are not equivalent to experimental confirmation of binding or activity.
references.approval: curator selection of 2026-10-08

references.label: Myosin lever swing
references.title: The lever arm swings 34 nanometres on one motor domain.
references.paper: Swinging lever mechanism of myosin directly shown by time-resolved cryo-EM
references.mechanism: The motor domain stays bound to actin while its lever arm swings from the primed position to the post-stroke position. The end of the lever moves about 34 nanometres.

references.label: Acoustical activity in a chiral lattice
references.title: A chiral lattice turns the polarisation of a wave as the wave travels.
references.paper: Ultrasound experiments on acoustical activity in chiral mechanical metamaterials
references.mechanism: A transverse wave moves through a lattice of chiral unit cells. The direction of the displacement rotates round the direction of travel.

Panel c: the unit cell that causes the rotation, with its dimensions.

references.check: Does the abstract panel have the same orientation and the same colours as the element in the real view?
references.limit: The lattice behind the column is busy. The phase wheel is cyclic and is hard for some colour-blind readers.

references.mechanism: A relaxation-driven transition propagates through a structured sheet; coupling its local shape changes to linkages produces spatially sequenced transport and actuation.

references.label: AlphaTensor
references.title: Matrix multiplication is a 3D block of ones and zeros.

references.mechanism: The product of two 2 by 2 matrices is a 4 by 4 by 4 tensor of zeros and ones. An algorithm for the product is a decomposition of this tensor into rank-one terms, and fewer terms mean fewer multiplications.

Below: a block of 4 by 4 by 4 cells, drawn as four separate slices. The axes are the entries of a, b and c.
A purple cube at (a, b, c) means that the product of that a and that b contributes to that c.

references.borrow: Draw a tensor as a block of cells. Separate the slices. Fill only the cells that carry information.
references.check: Can the reader read one cell and say what it means?

references.title: Give an object’s nonlocal effects their own visible layer.
references.paper: Generative Omnimatte: Learning to Decompose Video into Layers
references.authors: Lee, Lu, Rumbley, Geyer, Huang, Dekel & Cole
references.mechanism: Video is decomposed into object-associated RGBA layers that include effects such as shadows/reflections; removal-conditioned videos and a clean background support layer reconstruction.

references.avoid: Do not draw triangles merely because the method contains three modules.
references.limit: These arrows describe computation, not experimental causal evidence or a guarantee that every geometric constraint is satisfied.

references.label: Neural Congealing
references.title: Use an edit as a probe of correspondence.
references.paper: Neural Congealing: Aligning Images to a Joint Semantic Atlas
references.mechanism: A shared atlas maps corresponding semantic parts into common coordinates despite pose and appearance changes.
trace: Read one column from original butterfly to aligned butterfly.
Read across the aligned row: corresponding parts occupy common coordinates.
Inspect the transferred edit below: it follows the corresponding part back into each original pose.
references.lesson: Original, aligned and edited images form consistent rows with each specimen in the same column. A localized edit visibly follows the corresponding semantic part.
references.borrow: To show invariance, carry a concrete, localized probe through the transformation and back.
references.check: Does the probe remain attached to the intended feature? Include failures and cases outside the fitted regime.
references.avoid: Consistent coloring alone is not proof of a correct correspondence.
references.limit: Selected successes demonstrate correspondence qualitatively; they do not establish reliability over all inputs.

references.label: Aardvark
references.title: Evidence stays attached to the event it explains.
references.paper: Aardvark: Composite Visualizations of Trees, Time-Series, and Images
references.mechanism: Lineage, measured change and microscopy evidence describe the same cells and events but answer different questions.
trace: In b, the tree provides the structure; the orange trace lives inside each branch's lifetime.
The purple cell images are attached to specific points on that trace.
Compare c and d: changing the question changes which modality supplies the main layout.
references.lesson: Tree, measurement and image motifs remain identifiable when one becomes the host layout. Repeated colors communicate modality roles; nesting communicates event ownership.
references.borrow: Join modalities by entity and event before choosing how to compose their visual representations.
references.check: Can a reader inspect the raw evidence for a suspicious event without searching another panel? Validate every time/entity match.
references.avoid: Co-location is not enough: a screenshot near a curve must correspond to the same event.
references.limit: Figure 1 presents a design grammar, not experimental proof. Different host layouts do not imply that all modalities use one metric coordinate system.
